meta.method: Depth pass on everyday-garment brands that already had 1-2 products in the existing research-clothing-*.json files (Levi's, Gap, Banana Republic, J.Crew, Uniqlo, H&M, Zara, Mango, COS, Massimo Dutti, Abercrombie & Fitch, American Eagle, Hollister, Ralph Lauren, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Lacoste, Boden, Next, Marks & Spencer, Primark, River Island, Dunnes Stores, Reitmans, Roots, Aritzia, Liverpool MX, Suburbia MX). J.Crew, Gap and Banana Republic category/product pages rendered enough server-side HTML for WebFetch to read directly, so those entries are 'confirmed': true, source 'brand product page, fetched directly'. Uniqlo, H&M and COS are JS single-page apps: WebFetch timed out on Uniqlo and H&M (60s) and returned HTTP 403 on COS (cosstores.com/cos.com both), so those entries come from a WebSearch result snippet that quoted the brand's own product page price verbatim, confirmed:false. Zara, Mango, Massimo Dutti, Abercrombie & Fitch, American Eagle, Hollister, Ralph Lauren, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Lacoste, Boden, Next, Marks & Spencer, Primark, River Island, Dunnes Stores, Reitmans, Roots, Aritzia, Liverpool (MX) and Suburbia (MX) were not independently fetched in this pass (WebFetch was not attempted or was not needed because the search snippet already quoted a single unambiguous price tied to a specific product-page URL); those are also confirmed:false with the snippet noted as source. Every price is the exact figure shown in the fetched page or the quoting snippet, in its own currency, never converted. Levi's was targeted but returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt and search snippets only gave the women's jeans landing page with no single-product price, so no Levi's entry could be built honestly this pass.
dropped: Levi's (US): levi.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; search snippets gave only category/landing pages, never one product's own price, so no entry was built.

Penneys (IE): Primark/Penneys share a platform but no Penneys-specific (.ie) product price was found separate from the GB entries used here, so Penneys was not given its own line to avoid implying an IE price that was never read.

A COS 'Argyle wool-alpaca v-neck jumper' at £119 was dropped: the search snippet that quoted that price returned product-page URLs for a differently-named 'Alpaca-Wool Jumper', so the name and the price could not be tied together honestly.

A Liverpool (MX) 'Banana Republic polo neck sweater for men' at $1,070.30 was dropped: the link list under that search returned only a generically-titled product page ('Sueter cuello polo para hombre') with no brand name in the title or URL, so the brand attribution in the search summary could not be verified.

A COS 'Pure cashmere funnel-neck jumper' at £199 was dropped: the only product-page URL found for it was on the en-us path, which conflicts with the £-denominated price quoted for the UK site, and no GB-path URL for the same product code was confirmed.
